reason: A keeps the original stack (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal at the bottom) with sensible spacing. However, both decorative circles were shrunk into floating discs that no longer bleed off the edges, so the teal one crowds the can's right shoulder and looks arbitrary, and the legal line is very small. B puts the logo and the can right on top of the huge teal circle and shrinks the can. Its legal line floats mid-canvas over the blue circle with about 100px of empty space below it, so the bottom of the layout is unbalanced.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark is jammed against the bottle cap and the top edge, the subcopy and CTA label are too small to read at banner size, the headline floats in a big empty middle, and the two circles are pushed into the right corners with the yellow one cropped. B: text is large and readable and the order runs logo, bottle, headline, CTA, but it is cramped. The bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, the circles are stacked into one lump that crowds the end of 'fizz', the subcopy wraps to three lines and sits tight against the CTA, and the CTA is close to the right edge.

A has no collisions, but the hierarchy is broken. The 'Reserve a Case' CTA is a tiny pill in the right column, about the same size as the illegible legal text, while the left body copy is oversized and outweighs it. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone, and the orange divider has shrunk to a stray fragment. B is unusable: the headline's last line runs into the body copy, the orange divider strikes through 'Orange Zest and Smoked', and the SOLSTICE wordmark is jammed into the eyebrow, so the core message can't be read.

A rewraps the headline into four bold lines that fill the portrait width, so it dominates and the CTA sits close beneath it. Its main flaw is that the whole block sits low: about 170px of empty space at the top against about 50px under the button, which makes it bottom-heavy. B keeps the landscape two-line wrap at a small size, so the headline lines run almost to the side edges while large dead areas sit above and below. The gap between headline and CTA is also too wide, so B looks like a shrunk copy, not a layout redesigned for portrait.

A has a clean shared left edge and a logical brand→headline→sub→pills→CTA order. Its flaws: the headline wraps with an orphaned 'here', the right half of the canvas is dead space, and the peach circle in the bottom-right floats with no connection to anything. B's headline is oversized and runs almost to the right edge. Its left edges don't line up (wordmark and subhead at about 76px, headline at about 64px), the CTA sits off to the right, wedged between the subhead and the pills, and the flavour pills are pushed to the bottom below the button, so the reading order and grouping fall apart.

A reads left to right as a banner should: brand and headline on the left, date in the middle, and a prominent RSVP button grouped with its URL on the right. Its flaws: the can graphic floats awkwardly at the top centre, the headline is undersized for the format, the legal line sits right under the subtitle, and the missing-asset placeholder is still visible. B shrinks the RSVP button to a pill the same size as the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS badges, which buries the CTA. The two-line 'Sunset / Sessions' headline crowds against those pills, the subtitle is squeezed into a narrow, ragged column, the logo wordmark looks broken ('SOLST CE'), the legal text is tiny and stuffed into the right side, and the placeholder overlaps that corner.

A is broken. The 'See the Schedule' CTA is jammed against the bottom edge and partly cut off. The fine print crowds up against the button. The logo is wedged against the book cover's edge, and the text runs almost edge to edge with no margins. B is a sensible banner split, with the book on the left and the card on the right holding a clear headline and CTA. Its flaws: the logo has shrunk until it is illegible, the card runs flush to the canvas edge on the top and right, and the book sits small and loose on the confetti.

A has a clean headline and a strong CTA, but the price cards are shrunk to tiny thumbnails. Their plan labels and sublines can't be read, and the order is shuffled to 6/80/48, so Yearly is no longer the highlighted middle card. The right-hand column puts the subtitle and the fine print, which is set almost as large, in one cramped block pressed against the right edge, and the logo is very small. B is broken: the headline wraps to an orphaned 'week' that collides with the subtitle, and the Yearly card's '48' and 'per year' overflow below the dark tile onto the light background, where the cream text is almost invisible. B's subtitle and fine print are also jammed into a tiny, unreadable cluster.

I'd pick B, though neither is ready to ship. A: the big teal circle sits behind the GLACIER logo and the top of the can, the legal line runs over the light-blue bottom circle, and the logo is pushed down to y≈128, which leaves empty space at the top and below the CTA. B keeps the logo, can, headline and CTA in a clean central stack with good spacing. Its weaknesses: both circles were shrunk into small floating dots that no longer bleed off the edges as in the original, the teal circle touches the can's right green dot, and the tiny legal line nearly touches the bottom circle.

A reads well as a left-to-right banner (logo, bottle, headline, CTA) with a strong headline and CTA. Its flaws: the right edge is cramped, with 'fizz' and the oversized CTA crowding the overlapping decorative circles; the headline is jammed near the top edge; and the body copy wraps awkwardly into three lines. B has clear defects. The SOLSTICE logo is crammed against the top edge and collides with the bottle cap, and the bottle nearly touches the bottom edge. The subcopy and CTA label are too small to read comfortably, and wide dead gaps leave the elements looking scattered.

A has severe collisions. The headline's last line sits on top of the body copy, the orange divider strikes through 'Smoked Rosemary', and the eyebrow crowds the logo, so the main message can't be read. B has no collisions and a readable headline, but the 'Reserve a Case' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable chip while the body copy is huge, which turns the hierarchy upside down. The eyebrow is missing, and the legal text and 'Ships late June' are illegibly small.

A: the headline is set too small for the portrait canvas, and its two long lines nearly touch the side edges. The gap of about 115px between headline and CTA breaks them into two groups, and large dead bands sit above and below, so it reads like a shrunk copy rather than a recomposed layout. B: the headline is enlarged and rewrapped to four lines, with strong hierarchy, and the CTA sits close to it, matching the original. However, the block sits low: the top margin is about 170px but the CTA is only about 50px from the bottom edge, so it needs a small upward nudge.

A: the left edges don't line up. The headline starts at about x=64 while SOLSTICE, the subhead and the pills start at about x=76. The headline runs to within about 30px of the right edge. The CTA floats on the right between the subhead and the pills, so it breaks the reading order and isn't grouped with anything, and the space below the pills is left dead. B: one clean left axis and a logical order (brand, headline, subhead, flavour pills, CTA). But the headline is squeezed into about half the width, which leaves 'here' orphaned on its own line, and the right half and bottom are mostly empty apart from the pink circle.

A: the RSVP button has shrunk to the same size as the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills, so the CTA is buried in a row of badges. The logo wordmark looks broken ('SOLST CE'), the tagline is stuck in a narrow centre column wedged between the headline and the date, and the legal text and partner mark are tiny scraps in the corner, so the layout is jumbled. B: it uses clear columns (brand and headline, then date, then pills and RSVP), and the CTA stands out. However, the headline is fairly small and competes with the RSVP button, the can graphic floats loosely in the middle, the legal line sits right on the bottom edge, and the missing-asset placeholder is clearly visible.

A uses a sensible banner split, with the book on the confetti at left and the card with a dominant headline at right. However, the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an illegible speck, the card runs flush against the top and right canvas edges, and the free-entry note is tiny and crammed beside the CTA. B's CTA button is cut off by the bottom edge, and the card itself runs off the canvas. A confetti piece collides with the free-entry note, the headline is undersized relative to the rest, and the book and logo crowd the top of the card, leaving no breathing room.

A is broken. The headline's second line, 'week', runs into the subtitle. The '48' and the cream 'per year' text spill out of the dark card onto the light background, where they become unreadable. The 'per month' and 'up to 5 people' lines also sit outside their cards, and the legal text is jammed under the subtitle. B has a clear, dominant headline and CTA, but the three plan cards are shrunk to thumbnails with illegible labels and they are out of order (6, 80, 48). The subtitle and legal copy are crammed into a tiny block at the right edge, and the logo is undersized. B is flawed but much less broken than A.

A keeps the original layering, with the green circle bleeding off the top-right behind the bag. The headline is large and dominant, but it wraps to leave 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the gap between headline and CTA is tight compared with the space above. B shrinks the wordmark, headline and especially the CTA label, which becomes tiny and hard to read. It also strands both circles as floating blobs in the bottom third, so dead space opens around the headline and the bleed-off-edge feel of the original is lost.

A works as a left-to-right banner: the large serif headline is clearly the main element and the CTA sits at the right. However, the logo, tiny can and tilted badge are crammed into the left third, the badge is pushed into the bottom-left corner, and the legal text under the CTA is almost as heavy as the button label. B has its hierarchy upside down: the headline is tiny and about the same size as the legal text, while the badge and CTA overpower it. Its can is jammed against the left edge with the SOLSTICE label spilling out of it, and the decorative circles are cut off at the edges.

A: the circle runs right to the top and bottom canvas edges. The GLACIER wordmark floats centred over nothing instead of lining up with the headline's left edge. The two badges and the CTA sit as a heavy cluster in the bottom-right corner, jammed against the edge, with dead space above them, so the right column is lopsided. B: GLACIER, the one-line headline, the body copy and the badges share a clean left edge, and the CTA stands alone on the right as a clear end point for a left-to-right read. However, there is a big empty gap between the headline and the body copy, the badges almost touch the bottom edge and are nearly as large as the CTA, and the CTA crowds the right margin.

A breaks the headline badly, leaving 'sunshine.' alone on the second line. It also left-aligns the CTA at the edge under a centred headline, so the alignment is mixed, and the LIMITED badge is enlarged and pushed to the right, which makes the group look arbitrary. B keeps the original's centred structure with a balanced two-line headline and the badge+CTA group. Its flaws: the headline is crammed near the top with a big empty band at the bottom, the CTA sits tight under the headline, and the badge+CTA group is still off-centre to the left.

A shrinks everything instead of rearranging it. The CITRINE logo and the 'Find a Store' label are tiny and hard to read, the content sits in the upper two-thirds with a dead gap under the product, and both circles are moved to the bottom as small, unrelated blobs, so the original's layering of the green circle behind the bag is lost. B keeps the green circle behind the bag as in the original, uses the tall canvas well and keeps text readable, but the headline breaks onto two lines with 'fizz' left alone on the second, the CTA sits too close under the headline, and the olive circle crowds the bottom-left corner.

A: the can is pushed against the left edge and its 'SOLSTICE' label spills past the can, the standalone logo is gone, and the headline is tiny, barely bigger than the two-line legal text. The CTA ends up as the only focal point, so the hierarchy is wrong. B: the large two-line headline clearly leads and the logo is kept, but the tilted sale ribbon is clipped at the bottom-left edge, the can is shrunk to almost nothing, and the legal text is crammed into three lines under the CTA, close to the bottom edge.

A has a sensible left-to-right flow: product circle, then left-aligned text column, then the CTA on the right. But there is an awkward empty gap between the one-line headline and the body copy, the pills are jammed close to the bottom edge, and the can label is now illegibly small. B's GLACIER wordmark floats centred and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge, and the circle nearly touches the top and bottom edges. B's pill text is also tiny, and its right-hand pill and CTA block crowds the bottom edge, so it reads less deliberate than A.

A keeps the original's centred headline, balanced two-line wrap and LIMITED-badge/CTA grouping. However, the whole block sits high: there is a tight top margin over a large empty band at the bottom, and the badge+button pair is still slightly off the headline's centre axis. B wraps the headline into an orphaned single word, 'sunshine.', and pushes the CTA hard left against a centred headline, so the alignment axes conflict. It also enlarges the LIMITED badge and leaves it floating in the middle, which loses the original's deliberate grouping.

A has a clear left-to-right banner flow: copy on the left, the product in the centre, the CTA on the right. But the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to a speck sitting on a decorative circle, the sale ribbon is jammed against the left edge and nearly touches the headline, and a large empty band runs between the product and the CTA. B blows the headline up so far that it crowds the bottom edge and overpowers everything else. Its product bottle shrinks to a token icon in the top-right corner, sitting on a decorative circle. The sale ribbon floats unanchored in the middle, and the subcopy, CTA and legal text are crammed into a tight right column, so the hierarchy and balance are lopsided.

A: the headline is strong and the hierarchy holds, but the alignment is mixed. GROVE is centred, the headline and body copy are left-aligned, and the badges and CTA are pushed to the right. The two badges nearly touch, and the shoe spills past the edges of the circle. B: the headline is shrunk and weak, and GROVE is tiny. There is an odd gap between the headline and the body copy, which leaves 'bottles.' orphaned on its own line. The FREE DELIVERY badge has been moved off its corner and dropped beside the chips. The CTA is undersized, and about 140px of dead space is left at the bottom.

A keeps the original's centred stack, palette and hierarchy intact, but it is basically the banner dropped onto the square. The block sits high (about 190px above it and 270px of empty orange below), so the bottom feels dead, and the subcopy is small for the format. B fills the square with a dominant headline, but the four-line break leaves 'Bubbles,' as a short top line. Its bottom row breaks the centred axis: the subcopy is a centre-aligned, ragged three-line block (with 'Now in' / 'four flavours' split) next to a right-pushed CTA that doesn't line up with the headline edges. That row also sits cramped near the bottom edge.

A has a clean vertical stack and nothing collides, but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The body copy also wraps to leave 'sparkling.' alone on a line, and the centred bottle and CTA don't line up with the left-aligned text block. B is unusable: the bottle sits on top of '20% off' and covers 'case of' in the body copy, and the whole content block hangs in the middle with the bottom third of the canvas left empty.

A has a clear left-to-right banner structure with the headline and subcopy vertically centred and the CTA on the right, but the phone runs almost the full canvas height and nearly touches the top and bottom edges. The tilted 'ONLINE ONLY' badge, stacked under 'Try It' at nearly the same width, reads as a second button and weakens the CTA. B gives the CTA strong prominence and keeps the original badge-beside-button pairing, but the headline is jammed near the top edge. The badge and button cluster in the bottom-right while the space under the subcopy sits empty, and the phone and circle crowd the top-left, so the whole layout feels cramped and top-heavy.

A keeps the original's left-to-right order (product circle, then headline, subline and CTA) with a clean left-aligned text column and clear hierarchy. Its flaws are small: the headline sits tight to the right edge, and the circle almost touches the top and bottom edges. B breaks the reading order by putting 'Out now.' after the button. Its oversized 'Try It' pill butts against the bottom of the product circle, and the right side is jammed into a cluster while the headline floats alone on the left with a dead gap between them.

A is mostly a scaled-down copy of the original. The hierarchy and the spacing between headline, details, chips and CTA all hold up, but the chip text and the URL line are small, the lower third is mostly dead space, and the red 'missing asset' placeholder is still there. B has real collisions. The can graphic sits on top of 'Pier 9'. The subtitle is jammed against 'Saturday 21 June' with no gap. All the content is crammed into the top 60% of the canvas, which leaves a large empty bottom half with only the placeholder box in it.

In A the product bottle, the original's centrepiece, is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed into the top-right corner on top of a decorative circle. The oversized headline nearly touches the bottom edge, the legal text is almost as large as the subcopy, and the ribbon floats on its own between the two columns. B keeps the left-to-right flow (copy, then the bottle at a sensible size, then the CTA), but the ribbon is crammed between the tiny logo and the headline with almost no gap. The CTA also floats at the right edge, cut off from its copy, and leaves a dead band above the legal line.

A: the headline is shrunk to one weak line that is too small for the canvas, and there's an odd large gap between it and the body copy. The FREE DELIVERY tag is dropped into the badge row, where it reads as a stray third badge, and the bottom ~140px is dead space. B: the headline is large and the stack is well filled, but alignment is mixed: GROVE is centred, the headline and body are flush left, and the badges and CTA are pushed right. The two badges almost touch, so the lower block looks ragged rather than built on a grid.

A rebuilds the layout for the square, and the four-line headline fills the canvas with strong hierarchy. But the subhead and CTA are squeezed side by side at the bottom: the subhead is centred, wraps awkwardly ('Now in / four flavours') and doesn't share an edge with the headline or the button, so the bottom row looks improvised. B is a clean, faithful copy of the original, but it is just the banner layout dropped in unchanged, sitting too high with a big empty band below (about 190px above vs 270px below), and the headline is undersized for the square, so it reads as an unadapted copy.

A: the bottle sits on top of the body copy and covers 'case of', which makes it unreadable. The '20% off' headline also runs into the bottle, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty, so it is clearly broken. B: nothing collides and it stacks top to bottom properly. But 'WEEKEND ONLY' has dropped below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order, 'sparkling.' wraps onto a line by itself, and the centred bottle and button don't line up with the left-aligned text, so it needs fixes before it can ship.

A: the CTA and the 'Online Only' badge are pushed into the bottom-right corner. The button is almost touching the bottom edge and the badge crowds it, leaving a large empty patch top right, so the layout feels bottom-heavy and stacked rather than read left to right. B keeps the original left-to-right banner flow, with the phone, a vertically centred text block and the CTA column. But the rotated badge is wedged under the button with only a few pixels between them, it sits close to the bottom edge, and the badge now competes with the CTA instead of leading into it.

A breaks the original's reading order. 'Out now.' is pulled away from the headline and parked beside the button, and the button sits almost against the bottom of the product circle. The headline floats alone on the left while the right side is crowded, so the layout is lopsided. B keeps the original structure: the product circle on the left and a left-aligned stack of headline, subtext and CTA. Its only flaws are minor: the circle runs very close to the top and bottom edges, and the headline's right margin is tight.

A: the can graphic runs into the 'Pier 9' address line. The subtitle's orphaned 'of the year' sits right against 'Saturday 21 June' with no gap, and everything is packed into the top half, leaving the bottom ~40% as dead space. B keeps the original's spacing and hierarchy with no collisions, but it is basically a scaled copy: the date, pills and can sit off-axis while the headline and CTA are centred, there is still empty space at the bottom, and the broken partner-logo placeholder remains.

A reads cleanly left to right: the can sits inside its circle, then brand and headline, then body copy with badges, and the CTA is prominent on the right. Its flaws are minor: the can is very small, and the badges are jammed against the body copy. B splits the can from its circle, leaving the circle clipped as an empty blob at the left edge and the can isolated at far right. B also puts the SOLSTICE wordmark below the headline, shrinks the CTA into a small pill that competes with the badges, and sets the body copy so small it can't be read. It also leaves a large dead gap between the copy and the can.

A reads left to right properly, with the phone, then brand and headline on one line, then the tagline and badges, then the CTA. Its flaws: the phone touches the top and bottom edges, which crops the circle; the CTA pill is far too tall, almost filling the banner height, and sits jammed against the right edge with its text crowded; and the badges compete with the headline for attention. B wraps the headline onto two lines, crowded right up to the top and bottom of the canvas. 'SOLSTICE' sits off to the left of the headline instead of above it, and the subcopy is too small to read. B also stacks the badges and CTA in a lopsided 2x2 grid: the CTA is the same size as the 'BACK BY DEMAND' badge, so it doesn't stand out, and 'SUMMER ONLY' floats on its own next to an empty slot. There is also a large dead gap between the phone and the text.

A is a clean vertical stack. The product sits centred in its lavender circle, and the copy below shares one left edge with sensible size steps and even spacing. Its only flaws are minor: the product now comes before the headline, and '20% off' could be larger for the tall format. B's text is crammed into the top third. 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' run over the cropped circle, the oversized CTA nearly touches the subhead with uneven margins, the can is stranded in dead space, and the fine print is far too large and competes with the message.

A: The text column shares a clean left edge and the headline > NEW > Try It hierarchy reads well. But the bottle sticks out of the cream circle at both the top and the bottom, the whole composition sits in the upper two-thirds and leaves a large dead orange band across the bottom, and the faint decorative circle at top right floats with no purpose. B: The product is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed into the top-left corner, with a clipped ghost circle behind it, so the key imagery is lost. The NEW badge is blown up to almost CTA size and competes with the headline and the button. The pills are right-aligned while the headline is left-aligned, so nothing shares an edge, and the button crowds the bottom-right margin.

A: the logo shrinks to an illegible speck in the top-left circle, and the legal line runs right into the placeholder box at bottom right. The phone and placeholder crowd that corner while the left-centre stays empty, and the headline is undersized for the banner. B: the headline is strong and the logo is clear, but 'Sunset Sessions' nearly touches the left edge, and '6 pm' is indented out of line with 'Saturday 21 June'. The middle column is cramped, with the legal text jammed under the URL, and the placeholder box floats on its own beside the phone.

A: the NEW VIDEO badge is jammed against the VOLTSTRIDE logo at the top, and the headline nearly touches the circle. 'Full review inside.' floats over roughly 150px of dead purple, so the composition is top-heavy and the lower third is empty. B: uses the vertical format better, with a large, dominant headline, a well-sized circle and the badge separated from the logo. However, 'Full review inside.' is jammed against the bottom edge and the circle, the left margin is tight, and the logo has shrunk noticeably.

A breaks the product apart: the green circle is cut off at the left edge while the can floats alone at the far right. SOLSTICE is placed under the headline, the CTA is a tiny pill crammed in front of the badges, and the body copy is too small to read. B is a proper leaderboard that reads left to right: the can sits in its circle, SOLSTICE runs above the headline, the copy and badges are in the middle, and a prominent CTA sits at the right. Its flaws are minor: the circle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, and the badges are tight under fairly small body text.

A: the phone is stranded far left with a big empty gap before the copy. SOLSTICE floats above and to the left of the headline instead of lining up with it. The CTA is stacked under a badge at the same width, so it reads as just another pill, and the right ~170px of the canvas is dead space. B: the layout reads left to right properly, with brand and a one-line headline, then subcopy and badges, then the CTA. However, the phone is cropped at the top and bottom edges, the CTA label is jammed against the sides of its pill, and the button sits tight to the right edge.

A blows the type up so far that '20% off' nearly touches the right edge. The top block is jammed, with the headline sitting across the cut-off circle, while the can floats alone in a large empty middle zone below the CTA. B neatly puts the can inside the full circle as a hero, with a clean left-aligned stack of eyebrow, headline, subcopy, CTA and legal text. Its only flaws are a slightly empty top band and a modest headline size.

A: the bottle badge is shrunk and jammed into the top-left corner, with its cap almost touching the edge, and the decorative circle is cropped. The NEW pill and Try It button are oversized and right-aligned, while the headline is left-aligned, so nothing shares an edge and the CTA competes with the headline. The lower-left is dead space. B: a clear two-column layout with a large hero bottle on the left, and the headline, NEW badge and CTA sharing one left edge with a sensible size order. But everything sits in the top two-thirds, leaving the bottom third of the canvas empty. The bottle spills well past its cream circle, and the faint stray circle top-right looks accidental.

A works as a left-to-right banner: the 'Sunset Sessions' headline is clearly the biggest thing and the RSVP button is strong. But the middle column is too tight, with the legal text pressed right under the URL line, and '6 pm' doesn't line up with 'Saturday'. The phone and the placeholder box are also squeezed against the right edge. B shrinks the logo into the top-left corner, where the faded circle runs over the sun icon. The headline is weaker, and the placeholder box at the bottom right overlaps the legal line and the canvas edge, so the fine print collides with it and gets cut off.

A is a proper vertical reflow. The headline is large and leads, the circle and shoe sit centred below it, and the logo and badge share a top band. Its flaws are small: the shoe runs slightly past the circle's left edge, and 'Full review inside.' sits close to the bottom edge with uneven spacing above it. B has clear faults. The NEW VIDEO pill is jammed against and clipped by the right edge, and the circle almost touches the headline above it. The 'Full review inside.' line floats on its own, and the bottom quarter of the canvas is left empty, so the layout feels top-heavy and unfinished.
